cs.name: Storage
cs.summary: Baskets, boxes and racks. Where the clutter actually goes.
cs.about: Clutter is rarely a space problem. It is a question of whether anything has somewhere to go. Baskets, boxes, racks and organisers that take what is already lying around and give it a place — chosen to be left out rather than hidden away, because storage that has to be tucked out of sight tends not to get used.

cs.name: Desk
cs.summary: The surface you work at, and what sits on it.
cs.about: The surface you work at deserves the same thought as the one you eat at. Lamps that put light where it is actually needed, organisers that keep a desk clear, and small objects that make sitting down to work feel deliberate rather than accidental. Most of it costs very little; all of it is in front of you for hours a day.

cs.name: Amphorae
cs.summary: Sculptural vessels inspired by timeless classical forms, crafted to bring elegance, character, and artistic depth to refined interiors.
cs.about: Amphorae bring the timeless character of classical vessels into contemporary interiors. Defined by their distinctive silhouettes, balanced proportions, and sculptural presence, these pieces work beautifully as standalone accents or as part of a curated arrangement. Whether placed on a console, sideboard, shelf, or dining table, amphorae add an understated sense of elegance, history, and artistic character to the space.

cs.name: Entryway
cs.summary: Hooks, trays and mats. The first three feet of a home.
cs.about: The first three feet of a home set the tone for everything past them. Hooks, trays, mats and small landing surfaces that catch keys, post and shoes before they scatter across the house. It is the least decorated part of most Indian homes and the first thing every guest sees.

cs.name: Sculptures
cs.summary: Objects that earn a surface of their own.
cs.about: Our sculpture collection brings together expressive forms and artistic silhouettes designed to elevate contemporary interiors. Whether displayed on a console, shelf, sideboard, or as a standalone statement piece, each sculpture adds personality, visual interest, and a sense of curated sophistication to the space.

cs.name: Chandeliers
cs.summary: Statement lighting designed to illuminate your space while adding elegance, character, and a refined focal point to contemporary interiors.
cs.about: Our lighting collection brings together elegant chandeliers and statement fixtures designed to transform interiors. From contemporary designs to timeless silhouettes, each piece combines functionality with visual appeal, creating a warm, sophisticated atmosphere while serving as a striking focal point in any room.

cs.name: Luminaires
cs.summary: Ambient lighting designed to add warmth, character and style to your space.
cs.about: From statement pieces to subtle accents, explore lamps designed to transform the atmosphere of your home. Discover lighting that complements your space, adds warmth and brings your interiors to life.

cs.name: Timepieces
cs.summary: Timeless accents that bring character, balance, and function to your walls.
cs.about: Discover a curated collection of wall clocks designed to do more than keep time. From understated modern forms to distinctive statement pieces, our timepieces bring together function and visual character, adding a considered finishing touch to living rooms, bedrooms, studies, and beyond.

cs.name: Bath
cs.summary: Small fittings and holders that decide how a bathroom feels.
cs.about: A bathroom is decided by its smallest fittings. A soap dish that drains, a holder that does not rust, a mat that dries between uses — none of them expensive, all of them touched every single day. These are the pieces that separate a bathroom that works from one that merely exists, and almost none of them are what you are shown first.

cs.name: Kitchen
cs.summary: The drawer and the worktop. Things you reach for every day.
cs.about: The kitchen is the room that gets used hardest, and the things that make it work are rarely the things a shop puts at the front. Utensil rests, drying racks, oil bottles, jars that actually seal — small objects, most of them inexpensive, each one removing a daily irritation you had stopped noticing. Chosen for how they behave on a worktop, not how they photograph.

cs.name: Bedroom
cs.summary: Bedside, wall and floor. What the room is actually made of.
cs.about: A bedroom is made of very few objects, which is exactly why each one counts. Light within reach of the bed, a surface beside it, something on the wall and something underfoot. Quiet pieces, chosen for how a room feels at the end of a long day rather than how it looks in the middle of one.

cs.name: Occasional Pieces
cs.summary: Side tables, shelves and seats — the pieces that finish a room.
cs.about: The trade calls them occasional pieces: the furniture a room can live without, and never quite looks right without. The side table that takes a cup and a lamp, the bedside that keeps a book within reach, the shelf that turns a bare wall into a place for books and plants, the ottoman that seats one more. Rattan, fluted wood, carved pedestals, boucle and a bookshelf shaped like a tree — chosen to carry a room's feel as much as its things.

cs.name: Curated Wallscapes
cs.summary: Canvases for the wall you look at most.
cs.about: A wall carries a room's mood more than anything standing in it. These are printed canvases and framed pieces — some quiet, some loud — chosen for the wall you face from the sofa or wake up to.

cs.name: Festivities
cs.summary: Brass, flame and flowers for the nights the house is lit.
cs.about: Diwali is the one week a year every home is styled on purpose. These are the pieces that carry it: urlis to float marigolds and diyas in, crystal for tealights to shine through, light for the balcony and the mandir. Chosen to look as right on the table the week after as on the night itself.
